title: Policy mesh desync caused variant shadowing and capacity burnout
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: During a sustained capacity fluctuation in us-west, routing policy updates propagated inconsistently across the policy mesh. A subset of routers continued using an older policy that preferred a deprecated model variant; this caused concentrated traffic to a small pool of instances, triggering capacity burnout, amplified cross-region retries, and a transient increase in user latency and error rates.
timeline: 2026-03-01 02:12 UTC - first elevated p50 latency alerted on frontend routers; 2026-03-01 02:16 UTC - retries and 502s increased in us-west; 2026-03-01 02:19 UTC - Canary metrics showed mismatch between policy version hashes; 2026-03-01 02:25 UTC - mitigation: force-roll policy v2026-03-01b across affected routers; 2026-03-01 02:40 UTC - traffic rebalanced and error rate recovered to baseline. Post-incident analysis started same day.
impact: Customer-facing latency spike (p95 +420ms) and transient 3.4% failure rate for 18 minutes affecting hosted API keys in us-west region. Several downstream customers observed degraded throughput during the event, leading to support tickets and SLA noise.
root_cause: Policy connector component (policy-distributor) lacked a strong version-consensus/checkpoint mechanism. When a partial config propagation occurred during a scaling event, routers without the latest policy continued to prefer a deprecated variant (variant-shadowing). The mismatch amplified when capacity autoscaling lagged, concentrating load on a shrinking pool.
detection: Alerting surfaced elevated p50/p95 and increased 502s. However, there was no targeted alert for policy-version skew across the mesh. We discovered the skew after comparing policy version hashes from router traces and policy-distributor logs.
remediation: Immediate: Force-roll the canonical policy version to all routers and temporarily increase instance capacity for affected variant pool. Medium-term: implement durable policy versioning with UUID, TTL-based refresh, and an active mesh-consensus healthcheck. Add circuit-breaker for variant selection when local capacity falls below threshold.
action_items: (AISH-1) Add policy-version hash exposure to router /metrics for automated drift detection — owner: Marcus Liu — estimate: 3 — target: 2026-03-15
(AISH-2) Implement policy-distributor consensus checkpoint: leader-based commit + per-router ack with retry/backoff — owner: Daniel Kim — estimate: 8 — target: 2026-04-02

(AISH-3) Build variant-capacity-aware circuit-breaker in routing decision: fallback to broader variant set or default model when local remaining_capacity < 20% — owner: Sophie Hernandez — estimate: 5 — target: 2026-03-29
(AISH-4) Create an automated smoke test that simulates partial policy rollouts to validate mesh convergence under churn — owner: Elena Novak — estimate: 4 — target: 2026-03-22
(AISH-5) Instrument runbooks and add a dedicated 'policy-desync' incident playbook to Console runbooks — owner: Omar Rahman — estimate: 2 — target: 2026-03-18
(AISH-6) Dashboard: add a Policy Drift panel correlating policy-version diversity, router-level hashes, and per-variant QPS — owner: Marcus Liu — estimate: 3 — target: 2026-03-20
notes: We observed that deprecated variant tags were not garbage-collected for 48 hours in the policy cache — plan to add TTL and automated GC.
Customer impact communication: sent a follow-up to all impacted customers on 2026-03-02 with mitigation steps and timeline for fixes.
Post-incident retro highlight: need an explicit SLO for policy propagation time and a corresponding synthetic to validate propagation under load.
